tests.name: Quick Check
tests.description: Timed check on The Distribution of Income

questions.question: Explain two causes of income inequality in the UK.
questions.correctAnswer: Two causes: (1) Education and skills gaps — workers with higher qualifications earn significantly more. (2) Wage differentials — globalisation and technology have increased demand for high-skilled workers while reducing demand for low-skilled workers.

questions.question: Describe how government can redistribute income through taxation and spending.
questions.correctAnswer: Progressive income tax (higher earners pay 40% or 45% vs 20% basic rate) redistributes from rich to poor. Welfare benefits (Universal Credit, child benefit, state pension) provide income to those on low incomes. Free public services benefit the poor most.

questions.question: Evaluate whether reducing income inequality should be a government priority.
questions.correctAnswer: Argue for: inequality reduces social mobility, harms health and education, creates social tension. Argue against: some inequality provides incentives (to work harder, gain skills). Conclusion: reducing extreme inequality should be a priority, but some inequality is acceptable as an incentive — the key is ensuring opportunity and a minimum standard of living.

questions.correctAnswer: A grade 9 response will: explain the deficit (UK imports more goods than it exports); analyse causes (deindustrialisation, strong pound, low productivity); evaluate seriousness (deficit means living beyond means, financed by borrowing; but UK has services surplus and attracts investment); conclude: persistent deficit is concerning long-term but manageable short-term if the UK can continue attracting investment.
